name: bmg_nozzle
title: Back, Massier and Gier 45-15 deg conical nozzle: measured wall pressure (2D axisymmetric Euler, nozzle_axi)

reference.source: Back, Massier and Gier (1964), JPL Technical Report 32-654, Fig. 4 (tests 347, 348, 351), NASA NTRS 19650001801; digitized
Back, Massier and Gier (1964), JPL Technical Report 32-654, Fig. 4 (tests 347, 348, 351), NASA NTRS 19650001801; digitized
reference.shortfall: The inviscid value is 0.80 on both meshes (100 x 20: 0.806, 200 x 40: 0.799): not a mesh error. Cause not resolved: the report concludes that boundary-layer effects on the wall pressure were negligible (Conclusions, item 3), so a viscous effect is unlikely. At z = 2.24 in, just after the tangency of the 45 deg cone with the small throat arc, the measured pressure falls steeply (about -1.2 to -2.5 per inch), so an uncertainty of 0.03-0.05 in in the tap position or the digitized position equals the 0.07 difference, and the report finds tap-size effects of up to 7 % (Conclusions, item 4). A band that includes the position uncertainty (or the report's tabulated data, if they can be found) is recorded in the gap register.

study.title: Wall pressure along the nozzle
notes: Mesh: 8,000 cells, 4,229 iterations, converged yes, 150 s; discharge coefficient 0.9813.
RMS difference over all 19 measured points: 0.0210 (in p/p0).
Geometry from the printed dimensions; the profile's exit area ratio is 6.57 (the report rounds it to 6.63; the measured points end at z = 6.66 in, before the exit).
The test gas was heated air (1500 R) with a boundary layer; the solver is inviscid with gamma = 1.4 (the report's one-dimensional curve uses 1.40 as well).
